A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoEdit. All 12 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable and support comparison. The substantial revisions do not obscure the work's identity.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original GeoEdit experiments on ZsRE and COUNTERFACT, including editing performance, ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, and execution times.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original editing experiments, including additional baseline comparisons, backbone evaluations, general-ability retention tests, and layer ablations.

M1.justification: V1 computes angles and combines vectors in the autoencoder's latent space, then decodes the edited vector. V2 adds a t-SNE projection to two dimensions for angle calculation and applies the resulting editing decisions directly to the original task vectors (Sections 4.2–4.3, Equations 10–11). It also introduces GeoEdit*, combining AlphaEdit's MLP edits with GeoEdit on attention parameters.

E1.justification: ZsRE and COUNTERFACT remain the editing benchmarks. V2 additionally evaluates mathematical reasoning and broader knowledge retention on GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, and NLI (Appendix D.4, Table 10), substantially extending coverage beyond factual editing and its paraphrase/locality evaluations.

E2.justification: AlphaEdit, previously cited but not evaluated, joins the main comparison in Table 1. V2 also adds an evaluated in-context editing comparator, IKE, against F-Learning and GeoEdit on both editing benchmarks (Appendix D.6, Table 12). These additions materially broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: V1 distinguishes full-fine-tuning and LoRA variants; v2 describes GeoEdit and F-Learning as using LoRA. Appendix C changes LoRA targets from q_proj/v_proj to q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj/up_proj/down_proj. New evaluations introduce fluency/consistency metrics, GPT2-XL (1.5B), Qwen 2.5 (7B), LLaMA3 (8B), and IKE with 32 cosine-selected demonstrations. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds comparisons of PCA, direct t-SNE, and autoencoder-plus-t-SNE angle extraction; lower/middle/upper MLP-layer editing ablations; and direct analyses of post-edit general-ability degradation (Tables 7, 10, 11). V1's editing-strategy, manual-weight, latent-dimension, lambda, and angle-threshold analyses are retained, with the former Appendix D sensitivity discussion moved to D.7.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental run counts or seeds, or reports standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The retained exponential moving average concerns the editing algorithm, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds AlphaEdit, GeoEdit*, IKE, and the appendix result sets, while many matched numerical entries remain unchanged. Most separate LoRA-condition results disappear; the LLaMA2-7B/ZsRE values recur rounded in Table 7. Table 4 revises ZsRE times for ROME from 8736.6 to 2184.2 seconds and MEMIT from 3448.8 to 862.2, making MEMIT faster than GeoEdit's retained 1028.0 seconds. Figure 3 also changes the reported angle distributions. Changed method/settings descriptions preclude treating these as straightforward same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 10–11 substantively change the mathematical quantities used: angles are defined on two-dimensional t-SNE representations, while fusion operates on original task vectors instead of latent vectors. The metric definitions and autoencoder loss remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: V2's introduction adds an explicit claim of complementarity with locate-and-edit methods and emphasizes best performance among fine-tuning methods. The central geometric-editing and importance-guided-fusion contributions, the stated 7.4% locality improvement, and the conclusion remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the large-latent-dimension failure explanation with autoencoder training loss impairing subsequent t-SNE, and changes the efficiency interpretation from substantially faster to broadly comparable with locate-and-edit methods. It adds explanations concerning AlphaEdit's external data, complementary parameter regions, layer importance, general-ability tradeoffs, and IKE's practical limitations. The explicit limitations concerning old-data access and imperfect geometric separation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C removes v1's full-fine-tuning learning rate, batch size, gradient-accumulation settings, DeepSpeed configuration, and baseline-setting reference. Section 5.4 also drops the autoencoder/vector-editing time breakdown. V2 specifies expanded LoRA targets, a neuron-as-matrix-column definition, layer ranges, and IKE demonstration selection. These materially revise reproducibility information; hardware and the existing autoencoder dimensions remain documented.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the three-family taxonomy with a fine-tuning versus locate-and-edit organization, removes the dedicated meta-learning discussion and associated references, and adds works including gradient-partitioning research, StruEdit, and IKE. More substantively, the positioning expands from improving F-Learning to complementing locate-and-edit methods through different parameter regions. AlphaEdit itself was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, related work, dimensionality-reduction explanation, and experimental discussion. It renames Section 3 to Problem Statement, reorganizes Appendix D into seven subsections, and updates author affiliations. The overall introduction–method–experiments–conclusion structure and substantial portions of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn for t-SNE-based angle extraction and original-vector editing. Figure 3 changes from two histograms to a four-panel comparison of reduction pathways. Table 1 gains explicit paradigm grouping and revised highlighting/captioning, while six additional appendix tables present new evaluations. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates alone.

improvement.justification: Stronger comparators, direct general-ability tests (Table 10), and angle/layer ablations address important gaps in v1's validation and better expose tradeoffs. The benefit is limited by removed training details, unclear correspondence between new LoRA descriptions and retained full-fine-tuning scores, and new overstatements: D.3 claims wins across every metric, although Qwen 2.5 reliability is 74.37 versus F-Learning's 75.06 (Table 9). The added diagnostic evidence supports a modest overall improvement, without establishing a same-setting performance advance.
